airport.name: Al Ain Airport Ain District, Shabwah Governorate, Yemen

summary: Al Ain Airport (WDA) is a small domestic airstrip serving the Ain District in Shabwah Governorate, a sparsely populated region in central-eastern Yemen. The facility primarily supports limited regional connectivity, oil industry logistics, and humanitarian or governmental flights in this remote part of the Arabian Peninsula. Given the ongoing security situation in Yemen, commercial service is minimal and operations are often subject to changing conditions.
faqs:
Q: Does Al Ain Airport have regular commercial flights?
A: Scheduled commercial service is very limited or suspended; most flights are charter, humanitarian, or oil-industry related.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small regional airstrip, it offers minimal passenger amenities; travelers should expect basic infrastructure only.

Q: Is the airport safe to use?
A: Security conditions in Yemen change frequently; check current travel advisories from your government before planning any trip.

Q: Which city does the airport serve?
A: It serves Ain District and surrounding communities in Shabwah Governorate, including workers in the local energy sector.
transport_tips: Ground transport options are limited; arrange a private 4x4 vehicle in advance, as taxis and public transit to the airport are unreliable in this remote region. Road conditions in Shabwah Governorate can be rough, so plan extra travel time especially after dark. Many visitors arrive via connecting flights from Aden or Sana'a rather than direct international routes.
local_tip: Carry sufficient cash in Yemeni rials and fuel, as ATMs and petrol stations are scarce in the Ain District area, and plan all logistics well in advance given the limited infrastructure.
